title: How AI Answers Questions and Why Your Brand Should Care
excerpt: How ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini answer questions using training data and web search, and what that means for your brand's visibility.
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
## Quick Answer

AI assistants answer questions by [predicting text](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed), one token at a time, based on patterns learned from large amounts of training data. Many assistants can also search the web and use the retrieved pages to ground and cite their answers. Whether your brand appears depends on what the model learned in training and what it finds when it searches, which is why brands need to understand and measure both.

## Introduction

Your brand is being described right now by AI assistants you may never have checked. When potential customers ask ChatGPT or Perplexity which products to consider in your category, is your brand mentioned?

Instead of scanning a list of links, a buyer can ask an assistant and get a written answer, often with a shortlist of recommended products.

If your brand isn't part of those answers, those prospects may never consider you. Understanding how AI answers questions is the first step toward fixing that.

## What Is AI Question Answering?

AI question answering is the process by which an AI assistant interprets a question and generates a direct, conversational response, instead of returning a list of links.

Assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini are built on large language models (LLMs). According to [OpenAI's explanation of how its models are developed](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed), the model learns relationships in its training data, such as how words typically appear together, and uses that to predict the next most likely word, one piece (token) at a time. Most modern LLMs are based on the Transformer architecture, introduced in the 2017 paper [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762).

When you ask a question, an assistant typically:

1. Interprets the question in the context of the conversation
2. Decides whether it can answer from what it learned in training or should search the web
3. If it searches, retrieves relevant pages and reads them
4. Generates an answer that combines that information
5. Names brands or products that fit the question, often with citations when it searched

The key difference from traditional search is that users get an answer, not a list. They can get product recommendations without visiting a single website, and they often make a shortlist based on what the assistant chose to mention.

## How Do AI Platforms Like ChatGPT Answer Questions?

Answering a question involves several stages.

### Understanding the Question

The model processes your question as a sequence of tokens and interprets it in the context of the whole conversation, plus any instructions or saved preferences.

A question about "best running shoes" leads to a different answer than "running shoes for marathon training with wide feet," because the extra context changes what's relevant.

### Training Data vs. Live Retrieval

Every model has a training cutoff. What it knows "from memory" comes from data collected before that date. [OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) its models are trained on publicly available internet data, data accessed through partnerships, and data from users, human trainers and researchers.

To get beyond the cutoff, assistants use retrieval: they search for current information and feed it to the model before it answers. This approach is known as retrieval-augmented generation, described in the [original RAG paper by Lewis et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401).

All four major assistants can do this:

- **ChatGPT** can [search the web](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), automatically or on request, and shows citations to its sources. OpenAI notes it may rewrite your question into one or more targeted queries sent to search partners.
- **Claude** can [search the web](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search) on all plans and provides direct citations when it uses web information.
- **Perplexity** [searches the web and includes numbered citations](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work) linking to its sources in each answer.
- **Gemini** models can ground answers in Google Search results; Google documents this for developers as [Grounding with Google Search](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search).

### Which Brands Get Mentioned

We're not aware of any AI provider publishing a ranking formula for brand mentions. Based on how these systems work, the main influences are:

- **Presence in training data**: how often and in what context your brand appears across the public web
- **Third-party sources**: reviews, comparisons, news and expert articles that discuss your brand
- **Retrieved pages**: which pages the assistant finds when it searches for your category
- **Relevance**: how well your brand matches the specific constraints in the question
- **Conversation context**: the user's stated needs, budget and preferences

For a deeper look at sources, see [where does ChatGPT get its information?](/blog/where-does-chatgpt-get-its-information)

### Generating the Response

The model then writes an answer in natural language. For product questions, this often includes:

- A direct answer first
- Supporting context and explanation
- Brand recommendations with reasoning
- Comparisons where relevant
- Caveats or limitations

Because generation involves sampling, the same question can produce somewhat different answers on different runs, as [OpenAI notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed).

## Why Does How AI Answers Questions Matter for Your Brand?

Understanding how AI answers questions helps you see why some brands get named and others don't.

### The AI-Assisted Buyer Journey

People ask ChatGPT: "What's the best project management software for remote teams?" They ask Claude: "Which sustainable sneaker brands should I consider?" They ask Perplexity: "What CRM do startups use?"

If they act on the answer, a brand that isn't mentioned may never enter the buyer's consideration set.

### Brand Mentions Shape Shortlists

When AI mentions your brand positively, you gain:

- Inclusion in the shortlist
- Context for why you might fit the buyer's needs
- Exposure next to, or instead of, competitors

When AI omits your brand, prospects may choose from the brands it did mention.

### Traditional SEO Doesn't Guarantee AI Visibility

Ranking well on Google helps, especially for assistants that search the web, but it doesn't guarantee that ChatGPT or Claude will mention you. Answers also reflect training data and how often independent sources associate you with your category.

Your brand benefits from presence across:

- Respected publications in your industry
- Forums and communities where real users discuss solutions
- Review platforms with genuine customer feedback
- Industry reports and comparison articles
- News coverage and thought leadership

### Many Brands Aren't Measuring Yet

In our experience, many brands still don't track how AI assistants describe them. That gives teams that start measuring now a chance to find and fix gaps early.

## How Can You Track How AI Answers Questions About Your Brand?

Monitoring AI visibility requires systematic checks across multiple platforms.

### Step 1: Identify Your Critical Questions

List the questions potential customers ask when researching your category.

Examples:
- "What are the best [product category]?"
- "Which [solution type] do experts recommend?"
- "What should I look for in a [product/service]?"
- "[Your brand] vs [competitor] comparison"
- "Is [your brand] worth it?"

Focus on high-intent questions that signal buying readiness.

### Step 2: Query Multiple AI Platforms Consistently

Ask the same questions on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini. Responses can vary a lot between platforms.

ChatGPT might mention your brand while Claude doesn't. Perplexity might cite a recent article the others missed. Gemini might draw on different sources entirely.

Use a fresh conversation for each check, keep wording identical, and repeat the same questions monthly to track changes. Personalization features like [ChatGPT Memory](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt) can influence answers, so test from a neutral account where possible.

### Step 3: Document Brand Mentions and Context

Record when your brand appears, the context, sentiment and position relative to competitors.

Key data points:
- Was your brand mentioned at all?
- In what position (first, middle, last)?
- What reasoning did the AI give?
- Which competitors were mentioned alongside you?
- Which attributes or benefits were highlighted?
- Which sources were cited, if any?

### Step 4: Analyze Patterns Across Platforms

Identify which platforms mention you and which don't. Look for patterns in:

- Question types that trigger mentions
- Competitive positioning across different questions
- Sentiment differences between platforms
- Frequency of inclusion over time

### Step 5: Benchmark Against Competitors

Track competitor mentions using the same questions to understand share of voice. This shows:
- Where you're winning AI visibility
- Where competitors dominate
- Opportunities to improve positioning
- Gaps in your AI presence

Our guide to [AI share of voice](/blog/ai-share-of-voice) explains how to calculate it.

### Step 6: Measure Changes Over Time

AI models get updated, search results shift, and your visibility changes with them. Regular tracking shows:
- Whether your visibility is improving or declining
- The effect of PR and content initiatives
- Seasonal patterns
- New competitive threats

For a full walkthrough, see [how to track brand visibility in AI platforms](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms).

## What Questions Should You Ask About How AI Answers Questions?

### How accurate are AI answers about brands and products?

Accuracy varies by platform and topic. In our experience, assistants tend to be more reliable about well-known brands with a large online footprint. They can miss newer brands, give outdated details, or state incorrect information confidently, which is known as hallucination. OpenAI has published research on [why language models hallucinate](https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/). Regular checks help you find and address inaccuracies.

### Why does my brand appear on ChatGPT but not Claude?

Each assistant uses a different model with different training data and cutoffs, and each searches the web differently. Both [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) and [Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search) can search the web, but they may run different queries and find different pages. Consistent, accurate information across many independent sources improves your chances on every platform.

### Can I influence how AI answers questions about my brand?

Indirectly, yes. Publish clear, accurate content on your site, earn coverage in respected publications, and build genuine reviews and community discussion. These are the sources assistants learn from and retrieve. You can't directly control or pay for mentions in organic answers; OpenAI, for example, says [ads don't influence ChatGPT's answers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt).

### How often do AI answers change for the same question?

Answers can vary between runs because generation involves sampling, as [OpenAI notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed). Assistants that search the web can change when search results change, and answers can shift when providers release new models. Repeating the same questions over time shows real trends beyond one-off variation. See [does ChatGPT give the same answer to everyone?](/blog/does-chatgpt-give-the-same-answer-to-everyone)

### What happens if AI gives wrong information about my brand?

Document the inaccurate answers and, where available, the sources cited. Then correct the information at the source: update your own site, ask publishers to fix outdated articles, and make sure your listings and profiles are accurate. Answers based on live search can improve once the cited pages are fixed; answers based on training data may only change with a future model.

### Do AI platforms prioritize certain types of brands?

We haven't seen evidence of intentional favoritism, but in our experience brands with lots of independent coverage, reviews and discussion tend to be mentioned more often, simply because there's more material associating them with their category. Niche brands with strong community presence can still do well for specific questions.

### How do I know which AI platform matters most for my audience?

Ask customers how they research purchases, add an AI option to "how did you hear about us" forms, and check referral traffic from AI platforms in your analytics. Because usage differs by audience and buyers may use more than one assistant, it's worth tracking all four.

## What Does the Future Hold for How AI Answers Questions?

Here are developments already underway that affect brand visibility.

### Multimodal Answers

Assistants can include images and other media in answers. ChatGPT, for example, [can show product results with images](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) when a question has shopping intent. Clear product imagery and accurate product data matter.

### Personalized Recommendations

Assistants can use context like memory and custom instructions. OpenAI says [ChatGPT's shopping results](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) consider your query and context, such as Memory. "Best for you" answers make it important to be visible across many use cases, not just generic "best" questions.

### Commerce Inside the Conversation

As of October 2026, [OpenAI's help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) says ChatGPT can show product options with links to merchants, and an Instant Checkout option for some eligible products and merchants. For some purchases, the AI answer is becoming the point of sale, not just the research step.

### Voice Interfaces

Where assistants offer voice modes, recommendations may be spoken rather than read. A clear, distinctive brand name and a simple description of what you do help.

### Source Transparency

Assistants that search the web, such as [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) and [Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search), show citations. That makes the cited pages, whether your own or third-party, a visible and important part of your AI presence.
